title: burst-priority-queue-abuse-playbook-proposals
content:
Summary:

This document is a combined on-call log, incident review, and runbook proposal for a class of incidents where large concurrent bursts (often following leaked API keys or automated bot campaigns) saturate token budgets and upstream GPU pools. These incidents share common characteristics: token exhaustion for a small subset of tenants, tail-latency spikes across multi-tenant endpoints, and WAF rules that lag the attack signature.

Goals:
- Provide immediate, safe mitigations for oncall to buy time without broad customer impact.
- Outline a new lightweight priority-queue layer to protect critical tenants and preserve SLOs.
- Capture experiments, thresholds, and follow-ups for engineering teams.

Incident pattern observed (recurring):
- T0: Sudden increase in requests matching a small set of API keys (observed via token-usage telemetry).
- T0+1m: P50 latency increases ~2x; p95/p99 cross thresholds; per-route token/sec limits hit.
- T0+2–5m: Autoscaler triggers scale-up but GPU slots are noisy due to many tiny requests (hot-start overhead).
- T0+5–20m: WAF signatures begin to catch some traffic, but false positives cause collateral impact.
- T0+20m+: Manual key rotation or tenant throttling required; incident impact extends if mitigation not quick.

Detection signals (high-confidence):
- A single API key accounts for >30% of token/sec across a region for >60s.
- Rapid growth of short-lived sessions (session creation rate >> baseline, >10x).
- Token bucket depleting on per-tenant tracker: sustained negative refill delta across 1–3 mins.
- Sudden jump in 429s correlated with below-SLO p95 increase.

Immediate on-call playbook (fast, minimally invasive):
1) Triage: Confirm via Datadog dashboards and token-usage index (dashboard: /dashboards/abuse-token-burst). Post alert in #sre-oncall with brief summary and timestamp.
2) Short-term throttling: Apply a per-key temporary throttle rule: limit to 10 requests/sec or 1k tokens/min for the offending key(s). Use the control plane path: /api/admin/throttle-keys (requires SRE-admin role). Add a 30-minute auto-expire tag.
3) Priority routing: If available, shift the tenant to the "protected" lane (low-concurrency, reserved p99 capacity) via routing override: route-policy=protected-low-latency. This isolates the noisy key from shared pools while preserving other tenants.
4) Key rotation & customer contact: If key appears compromised, escalate to solutions-engineering to notify customer and request rotation. If unable to reach, use emergency revoke: /api/admin/revoke-key (log action in incident ticket).
5) WAF tuning: Push a temporary signature for the observed payload patterns (if signature confidence > 0.8). Add whitelist for known good customers to avoid collateral.

Why priority-queue?
- Current coarse rate limiting (global token buckets per tenant) either throttles too late or causes brittle autoscaler behavior.
- A lightweight priority queue can: accept requests quickly, mark low-priority work and delay/evict it under pressure, and guarantee a minimum share to critical routes/tenants.
- It enables graceful degradation: preserve high-value flows (support, billing APIs, admin endpoints) while shedding noisy background traffic.

Priority-queue design sketch (implementation proposal):
- Placement: edge proxy layer (fast), first-match rule before global token bucket.
- Queues: three priorities: high (0.1x capacity slice), normal (0.8x), best-effort (0.1x). Percentages are configurable per deployment.
- Admission: token-based admission tokens assigned per request based on tenant SLAs and current queue depth.
- Eviction policy: FIFO within priority, then LRU across best-effort. Reject with 429 + Retry-After when queues full.
- Backpressure signal: when best-effort queue fills >80% for 30s, emit an alert and temporarily tighten normal queue admission.
- Telemetry: expose per-queue occupancy, dequeue latency, and per-tenant preemption events.

Runbook snippets for priority-queue in action (oncall steps):
- If p95 latency > 2x baseline and best-effort queue > 75%: flip controller switch 'pq-mode=strict' which reduces normal admission by 25% for 5 minutes.
- If a single key saturates high-priority shares: move key to 'quarantine' (explicit small queue with 0.5 RPS max) and notify customer.
- If GPUs are starved and queue latency climbs: enable fast-evict of best-effort and send a rate-limit header with suggested throttle.

Experiment log (Feb 9–12 dry run):
- Hypothesis: A 3-tier PQ with 10/80/10 slices reduces p99 tail latency by 35% for protected tenants under synthetic burst (1M short requests in 10m).
- Setup: Synthetic client farm (k8s/circuit-farm) replaying historical key-leak traffic; two protected tenants pinned to high slice.
- Results: p99 latency for protected tenants reduced from 1.2s to 0.65s. Overall token throughput dropped by ~12% (lost best-effort work). GPU utilization smoothed; autoscaler churn reduced by 40%.
- Observations: Need tighter telemetry on queue-drop causes; some legitimate long-lived conversations were misclassified as best-effort.

Threshold recommendations (provisional):
- Key-specific throttle trigger: >500k tokens/min OR >40% of regional token/sec for >90s.
- Queue backpressure alert: best-effort occupancy >70% for 60s.
- Auto-quarantine duration: 30m with exponential backoff on re-enable (x2 up to 4h).

Open action items (owners):
- Build controller switch and admin UI: eng-platform (Samir Khan) — due 2026-04-01.
- Telemetry endpoints for PQ: observability (Leah Chen) — due 2026-03-20.
- WAF signature automation for rapid ML-based signature gen: secops (Priya Shah) — due 2026-05-01.
- Postmortem template update to include PQ metrics: eng-sre (Ethan Morales) — due 2026-03-12.

Post-incident notes from last customer-impacting event (INC-2026-342):
- What worked: temporary per-key throttle and emergency routing override prevented full regional degradation in ~18m.
- What failed: WAF took ~22m to reach high-confidence signatures; key rotation was delayed due to missing contact info for the tenant.
- Customer impact: two mid-sized customers saw increased 429s for background tasks; three enterprise customers experienced p95 latency bumps for 12–25m.

Communications guidance for oncall:
- Initial Slack post: short timeline + action taken + link to ticket + expected next update in 15m.
- If key rotation required: solutions-engineering lead should draft a notice explaining rotation steps and temporary mitigation.

Appendix: useful queries and dashboards
- Datadog token-usage query: index:tokens region:us-east-1 | top by api_key over 5m
- SRE dashboard: /dashboards/abuse-token-burst (contains per-tenant token/sec, queue occupancy, GPU backlog)
- Emergency CLI commands: /ops/cli/throttle-key --key $KEY --rps 10 --expire 30m ; /ops/cli/revoke-key --key $KEY --force

End notes:
This doc is intentionally a proposal and oncall companion. It should be iterated with eng-platform and observability before being treated as canonical runbook. Feedback welcome — please add comments or raise JIRA-PLAT tickets for scope changes.

Ethan Morales
eng-sre
